notes.overview: Discovery call with Brightline Logistics, which builds routes for fourteen depots in spreadsheets and an aging dispatch system. Their biggest pains are late customer notifications and manual re-routing, and IT needs the nightly warehouse file and single sign-on covered. Both sides agreed to a six-week pilot at three depots, with a proposal covering both pricing models due next Wednesday.
notes: Brightline runs fourteen depots and about three hundred drivers, building routes each morning from an overnight warehouse file in spreadsheets.
Customers only get a four-hour window the night before, so some depots field over two hundred where-is-my-driver calls a day.
Re-routing after a sick call or breakdown takes dispatchers up to an hour and happens a couple of times a week per depot.
Tom is fine with a nightly file drop for the pilot but needs single sign-on and wants the provisioning timeline in writing.
About eighty seasonal drivers make per stop pricing, roughly seven to ten cents a stop, the likely better fit.
The pilot covers Eastgate, Pine Hollow and the Harbor depot for six weeks, measured on depot calls, re-routing time and on-time windows.

chapters.gist: Both sides agreed on a six-week pilot at three depots with measurable success criteria and a proposal due next Wednesday.

The drivers page will accept a pasted list of phone numbers, and the notifications page will preview the real customer message.
The setup checklist has five items, collapses after three, and its progress should be visible to customer success in the admin view.
Copy will be plain, direct and warm, with verbs on buttons and exclamation marks reserved for checklist completion.

notes.overview: Readout of the first pricing page experiment, which defaulted the plan toggle to annual. The annual share of self-serve checkouts rose from 22 to 34 percent while checkout conversion held inside the guardrail, so the annual default ships with the redesigned page. The next test will be a cost estimator that helps visitors choose between per driver and per stop, run on the new flag service.
notes: Defaulting the toggle to annual lifted annual plan share from 22 to 34 percent, or 23 to 33 percent using first assignments only.
The quick split script reshuffled returning visitors into a 53 to 47 split, so sticky assignment is mandatory for future tests.
Checkout conversion moved from 3.1 to 3.0 percent, well within the guardrail of no more than a five percent relative drop.
Prospects now raise annual terms earlier, while a couple of small fleets found the default slightly pushy.
About a third of sales calls include confusion about per driver versus per stop, and unsure visitors tend to request demos.
Forecasts will use the lower bound of the effect, and refund and downgrade requests will be tracked for sixty days.

notes.overview: Triage of driver app sync failures at Fernhollow Grocers and Redwick Parcel, traced to a token refresh race introduced when login token lifetimes were shortened. No delivery data was lost, a server-side grace window ships today with an app fix to follow, and Redwick will be offered an SLA credit before they ask. Daniel owns customer communication and Priya will run a blameless postmortem.
notes: About forty Redwick drivers and fifteen Fernhollow drivers stopped syncing after the release that cut login token lifetime from twenty-four hours to one.
Concurrent token refreshes after offline stretches triggered reuse detection, which revoked sessions while the app kept queueing data locally.
No data was lost, and logging out and back in flushes the queue, which is the interim workaround for drivers.
A thirty-second grace window for reused refresh tokens fixes every app version server-side, and a single-flight refresh ships in the next app release.
Roughly nine hours of degraded sync breaches Redwick's 99.5 percent availability commitment, so a credit will be offered proactively.
Eleven other customers saw a few revoked sessions and will get a short proactive note once the fix is live.
Prevention work covers offline testing, a per-customer sync failure alert and staged rollouts for login changes.

notes.overview: The Q4 roadmap review set three themes, reliability, enterprise readiness and self-serve growth, with a rule that new work must displace existing work. The team agreed on a pricing and packaging update with three tiers and notifications included everywhere, a single sign-on beta in about four weeks, and a functional mobile phase one before customers' peak-season freeze. Audit logs were named as the first item to slip if the senior backend hire starts late.
notes: Reliability targets are 99.9 percent sync success, notifications within sixty seconds for 99 percent of events, and under four pages per on-call week.
Single sign-on blocks four deals worth about six hundred thousand in annual revenue, and a beta for two design partners is targeted in about four weeks.
Automatic user provisioning is explicitly kept out of the single sign-on promise to protect the timeline.
Per active driver and per stop pricing both stay, packaged into Starter, Growth and Enterprise tiers with notifications included in every tier.
Self-serve aims to lift trial to paid conversion from nine to twelve percent, mainly through the onboarding redesign.
The mobile refresh is limited to tap targets, the stop list and sync status before the peak-season freeze, with visuals moving to Q1.
Packaging changes apply only to new customers until January to avoid extra support load during peak season.
